summary: SPY fell about 2% (spy_value 571.60 to 560.38) and closed at 715.87, 1.9% below the 730.02 line, so the shared VOO/VTI price stop has now tripped on top of the RSP clause the PM recorded this morning. Nothing in the news input explains the selloff: no market-wide headline, no ETF-tagged story and no 8-K on any holding beyond WMT's. The day's only company event was WMT's confirmed Q3 print (8-K 2.02, beat and raised FY guidance). WMT fell 0.97% against SPY's 2%, so it was the book's best relative performer. That confirms yesterday's read that the 11-17 'Walmart Reports Q3' headline was a mis-summarized preview. The losses elsewhere came from price, not news. CARG (-6.4%) and EXEL (-3.6%, now 1.3% above its $65 stop) had no headline or filing in the 72-hour or 7-day window, so I can't attribute those moves to any event.

broken_theses.why: Its price stop has tripped: SPY closed at 715.87, below the stored 730.02 200-day line (-1.9%, stop block 'tripped'). The RSP 21-day clause was already met this morning. There is no news reason to wait. The input has no ETF headline, rate decision or policy item that would make this a one-day dislocation. Together with VTI it is about 23.3% of equity on this one condition (L9).

The same shared SPY 200-day stop tripped at the 715.87 close, after the RSP clause was met this morning. Mark-to-cost is -6.1%, still above the $345.20 cost clause, but the SPY clause alone invalidates it. Under the 11-17 pre-commitment it should be sold together with VOO.
